items.body_md:
On August 17, Judge P. Kevin Castel signed the memo endorsement at Dkt. 94 in *Hachette Book Group, Inc. et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 1:26-cv-03689 (S.D.N.Y.), terminating Samuel Rubinstein as counsel of record for all plaintiffs. The withdrawal is procedural and, on its face, routine — Rubinstein's motion (Dkt. 93, filed August 14) was unopposed and the memo endorsement disposed of it the same day it was entered on the docket. The client roster and the substantive posture are unchanged. What the withdrawal does not resolve, and what continues to ripen toward the September 15 initial conference before Judge Castel (Courtroom 11D, 3:00 PM), is the live dispute over plaintiffs' letter motion for leave to file a motion to strike (Dkt. 90, August 3) and Meta's responsive letter (Dkt. 92, August 7). Judge Castel has not yet authorized briefing on the motion-to-strike question; the September 15 conference is the next event where that authorization — and any direction on Google's transfer motion analogue in the related Gemini action — may materially advance both dockets simultaneously.

Also on August 17, Meta filed exhibits at Dkt. 810 in *Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:23-cv-03417 (N.D. Cal., Chhabria, J.), in compliance with the sealing order at Dkt. 805 governing materials submitted in connection with Dkt. 781. Six exhibit attachments were filed — Exhibits B, D, E, F, G, and H — by Phillip Morton. The filing is substantive in classification (it executes a court order on the scope of sealed materials related to prior merits briefing), but routine in the sense that it resolves no independently contested issue; it completes the public-record compliance exercise Chhabria directed and has no independent bearing on the contributory infringement amendment posture or the coordinated deposition schedule. The further case management conference docketed August 17 — listed without an attached minute entry in the RECAP record, consistent with 
CourtListener's last-updated timestamp of August 14, 2026, at 11:21 AM and last known filing date of August 13, 2026
 — means the August 17 CMC entry itself has not yet generated a public minute entry confirming what Chhabria directed. That minute entry, once posted, governs the deposition-sequencing and class certification / summary judgment coordination that the August 14 conference addressed, including the confirmed 4-hour cap on Mark Zuckerberg's deposition and the extension of the Rule 30(b)(6) deposition from 14 to 21 hours. The contributory infringement amendment — 
grounded in the allegation that when Meta downloaded copyrighted works from shadow libraries using BitTorrent, it simultaneously uploaded those works onto the torrenting network, enabling other network members to infringe plaintiffs' rights
 — remains the live pleading question pending further direction from Chhabria; the August 26 deadline for calendaring Zuckerberg's deposition in the related *Entrepreneur Media, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:25-cv-09579 (N.D. Cal.), is the nearest time-sensitive marker across the Chhabria cluster.

*Getty Images (US), Inc. v. Stability AI, Inc. et al.*, No. 3:25-cv-06891 (N.D. Cal., Thompson, J.), *Encyclopaedia Britannica, Inc. and Merriam-Webster, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc. et al.*, No. 1:26-cv-02097 (S.D.N.Y., Stein, J.), *Hachette v. Google (Gemini)*, No. 1:26-cv-05870 (S.D.N.Y., Preska, J.), and *Thomson Reuters Enterprise Centre GmbH et al. v. Ross Intelligence, Inc.*, No. 25-2153 (3d Cir.), recorded no docket movement. In the Getty action, the scheduling-modification dispute is fully submitted before Judge Thompson following the August 17 responses-due deadline; a ruling — granting or denying both Getty's leave motion (Dkt. 70) and the underlying request to modify the scheduling order (Dkt. 68) — remains the next concrete milestone there. In the Google Gemini action, the transfer motion remains under submission before Judge Preska. In the Third Circuit, the panel of Judges Restrepo, Montgomery-Reeves, and Bove continues to deliberate following the June 11 oral argument.

On August 14, Judge Thompson's chambers received the completed paper record on the dueling Local Rule 7-11 dispute in *Getty Images (US), Inc. v. Stability AI, Inc. et al.*, No. 3:25-cv-06891 (N.D. Cal.), when Stability AI filed its proposed order (Dkt. 72) formally requesting denial of Getty's administrative motion for leave to file a reply (Dkt. 70). That proposed order — submitted by Joseph Gratz — is the procedural capstone to a sequence running from Getty's August 6 motion to modify the case management and scheduling order (Dkt. 68) through Stability's August 10 opposition (Dkt. 69), Getty's August 11 leave motion (Dkt. 70), and Stability's August 12 opposition to that leave request (Dkt. 71). The responses-due deadline of August 17 has now passed without further filing, so the matter is fully submitted. Judge Thompson may rule without a hearing. The practical stakes remain those covered yesterday: 
dispositive motions are due March 12, 2027, with jury trial set for January 18 through February 9, 2028
 under the current scheduling order, and 
private mediation must be completed by October 19, 2026
. Any extension Getty obtains on the schedule expands the window to develop its direct copyright, DMCA §1202, and Lanham Act claims — the core surviving theories after the April 2026 motion-to-dismiss ruling. The weights-as-infringing-copies theory that 
the UK High Court rejected in November 2025, with Getty granted leave to appeal in December 2025
, remains live before Thompson as well, giving the scheduling outcome downstream significance beyond a simple calendar adjustment. A ruling from Thompson — granting or denying both the leave motion and the underlying schedule-modification request — is the next concrete milestone in this action.

In *Hachette Book Group, Inc. et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 1:26-cv-03689 (S.D.N.Y., Castel, J.), nothing new has docketed since the attorney withdrawal at Dkt. 93 on August 14, covered yesterday. The September 15, 2026 initial conference before Judge Castel remains the next fixed milestone (Courtroom 11D, 3:00 PM), where the transfer motion and the motion-to-strike dispute previewed in Dkts. 90 and 92 will receive direction.

In *Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:23-cv-03417 (N.D. Cal., Chhabria, J.), 
CourtListener's docket reflects a last-updated timestamp of August 14, 2026, at 11:21 AM, with the date of last known filing listed as August 13, 2026
 — consistent with the Zoom case management conference having concluded but no minute entry yet appearing in the publicly accessible RECAP record. That minute entry, once posted, governs whatever Chhabria directed on the contributory infringement amendment posture and the coordinated discovery schedule across the related actions. The August 26 deadline for calendaring Mark Zuckerberg's deposition — ordered in *Entrepreneur Media, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:25-cv-09579 — remains the most time-sensitive near-term marker across the Chhabria cluster and should be confirmed against the docket in the related actions before that date passes.

*Encyclopaedia Britannica, Inc. and Merriam-Webster, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc. et al.*, No. 1:26-cv-02097 (S.D.N.Y., Stein, J.), *Hachette v. Google (Gemini)*, No. 1:26-cv-05870 (S.D.N.Y., Preska, J.), and *Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence*, No. 25-2153 (3d Cir.), recorded no movement. The Google transfer motion remains under submission before Judge Preska; the Third Circuit panel of Judges Restrepo, Montgomery-Reeves, and Bove continues to deliberate following the June 11 oral argument.

On August 14, counsel for Stability AI US Services Corporation, Stability AI, Inc., and Stability AI, Ltd. filed a proposed order (Dkt. 72) asking Judge Thompson to deny Getty's administrative motion for leave to file a reply — the formal capstone to the dueling Local Rule 7-11 motion sequence that began when Getty moved to modify the case management and scheduling order on August 6 (Dkt. 68). The proposed order follows directly from Stability's opposition at Dkt. 71 (August 12), filed by Joseph Gratz, and completes the paper record on both the leave-to-reply question and the underlying scheduling-modification dispute. Judge Thompson now holds the administrative motion (Dkt. 70) under submission; she may rule without a hearing, and the responses-due date of August 17 has passed, so a decision is ripe. The practical stakes are real: the existing scheduling order sets 
private mediation completion by October 19, 2026, dispositive motions due March 12, 2027, and jury trial from January 18 through February 9, 2028
. Any extension Getty secures expands the window to develop its remaining claims — direct copyright, DMCA §1202, and Lanham Act — following Judge Thompson's April 2026 motion-to-dismiss ruling, which preserved the overwhelming bulk of the complaint. 
The UK High Court in November 2025 rejected the theory that Stable Diffusion's model weights are themselves "infringing copies" but found limited trademark infringement and passing off, with Getty granted leave to appeal in December 2025
; the appeal's outcome on the weights theory bears directly on the same theory before Thompson, giving the scheduling fight additional downstream significance for rights-holders.

Also on August 14, an attorney withdrawal was filed in *Hachette Book Group, Inc. et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 1:26-cv-03689 (S.D.N.Y., Castel, J.), as Dkt. 93. The docket entry identifies only the filing type; the withdrawing attorney's name is not confirmed in the available record. On its own this is a routine personnel change, but the timing — three weeks before the September 15, 2026 initial conference before Judge Castel — and the live procedural posture warrant noting. That conference (Courtroom 11D, 3:00 PM) is where the transfer motion and Meta's response to plaintiffs' pre-motion letter on a contemplated motion to strike (see Dkt. 90, plaintiffs' August 3 letter; Dkt. 92, Meta's August 7 response) will likely receive direction. Separately, Anna M. Rennich's notice of appearance on behalf of all plaintiffs (Dkt. 91, August 7) is already on record, and any disruption to plaintiff-side coverage from the withdrawal is therefore contained.

In *Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:23-cv-03417 (N.D. Cal., Chhabria, J.), the further case management conference proceeded via Zoom on August 14 at 11:00 AM as scheduled. 
CourtListener's docket for Kadrey reflects a last-updated timestamp of August 14, 2026, 11:21 AM
 — consistent with the conference having occurred — but no minute entry has posted to the publicly accessible RECAP record as of this briefing. The minute entry remains the controlling source for whatever direction Chhabria gave on the contributory infringement amendment posture and the downstream discovery schedule across the four related actions where he denied Meta's motion to quash on August 11 (Dkt. 807). Separately, in the consolidated related matter *Entrepreneur Media, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:25-cv-09579 (Chhabria, J.), a prior minute entry already on the docket reflects two concrete directives relevant to the group: 
Lu's custodial documents were ordered produced no later than August 12, and Mark Zuckerberg's deposition is to be calendared no later than August 26
. 
If the deposition date has not been set by the next case management conference, the Court will set the date at that time
. The Zuckerberg deposition deadline is the next concrete, time-sensitive milestone across the Chhabria cluster and should be tracked against the docket in the related actions as of August 26.

*Encyclopaedia Britannica, Inc. and Merriam-Webster, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc. et al.*, No. 1:26-cv-02097 (S.D.N.Y., Stein, J.), *Hachette v. Google (Gemini)*, No. 1:26-cv-05870 (S.D.N.Y., Preska, J.), and *Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence*, No. 25-2153 (3d Cir.), recorded no movement. The Google transfer motion remains under submission before Judge Preska. The Third Circuit panel of Judges Restrepo, Montgomery-Reeves, and Bove continues to deliberate following the June 11 oral argument, with no decision issued.

items.body_md:
Today, Judge Vince Chhabria convened the further case management conference in *Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:23-cv-03417 (N.D. Cal.), at 11:00 AM Pacific by Zoom videoconference, the time having been advanced by the clerk's notice filed yesterday (Dkt. 809). The operative framing document before Chhabria was the Joint Case Management Statement filed Wednesday by counsel for sixteen named plaintiffs including Richard Kadrey, Ta-Nehisi Coates, Sarah Silverman, and Jacqueline Woodson (Dkt. 808). No minute entry or text order from the conference has posted to the public docket as of this briefing; the minute entry, when it appears, is the controlling source for whatever scheduling or substantive direction Chhabria announced. The two live threads heading into the conference were the contributory infringement amendment posture and the downstream discovery schedule in the four related actions where Chhabria denied Meta's motion to quash on August 11 (Dkt. 807, covering Nos. 3:25-cv-09579, 3:26-cv-02333, 3:26-cv-03725, and 3:26-cv-04053); both were ripe for scheduling direction. The minute entry is the sole remaining milestone for today's proceedings and should be pulled as soon as it posts.

In *Getty Images (US), Inc. v. Stability AI, Inc. et al.*, No. 3:25-cv-06891 (N.D. Cal., Thompson, J.), Stability AI filed its opposition to Getty's administrative motion for leave to file a reply (Dkt. 71, August 12), completing the paper sequence on a disputed Local Rule 7-11 procedural point that opened with Getty's scheduling-variance motion on August 6 (Dkt. 68) and ran through Stability's opposition at Dkt. 69 (August 10) and Getty's leave motion at Dkt. 70 (August 11). The opposition was filed by Joseph Gratz on behalf of all three Stability AI entities. The substantive question underneath the dueling administrative motions is what scope of modification, if any, Judge Thompson grants to the existing case management and scheduling order — which sets private mediation completion by October 19, 2026, dispositive motions due March 12, 2027, and a jury trial window of January 18 through February 9, 2028. 
Judge Thompson denied most of Stability AI's motion to dismiss Getty's complaint in April 2026.
 
The only claim dismissed was Getty's DMCA CMI §1202(a) claim, for failure to allege intentional conduct, though Getty was granted leave to amend.
 That posture — nearly all claims surviving — gives the scheduling fight its stakes: any expansion of the briefing or discovery schedule directly affects how much ground Getty can develop before the dispositive-motion deadline. 
The UK High Court decided the parallel UK action on November 4, 2025, rejecting the "model weights as infringing copies" theory but finding limited trademark infringement on Getty watermarks reproduced in generated images; Getty was granted leave to appeal in December 2025.
 The appeal's outcome on the model-weights theory bears directly on the same theory Getty presses before Thompson. Judge Thompson's ruling on the leave-to-reply motion is the next concrete event in this action; responses on Dkt. 70 were due August 17, 2026, making a decision possible in the coming days.

In *Encyclopaedia Britannica, Inc. and Merriam-Webster, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc. et al.*, No. 1:26-cv-02097 (S.D.N.Y., Stein, J.), the memo endorsement filed August 12 (Dkt. 59) is the only movement since the previous edition. As noted, the document text remains unavailable on the public record; the docket sequence — Dkts. 56 through 59 spanning August 5–12 — is consistent with the court working through interim case management obligations that arise within the existing stay tied to summary judgment proceedings in the broader OpenAI MDL (No. 1:25-md-03143). Nothing in the available record alters that stay posture. *Hachette v. Google (Gemini)*, No. 1:26-cv-05870 (S.D.N.Y., Preska, J.), and *Hachette v. Meta (Llama)*, No. 1:26-cv-03689 (S.D.N.Y., Castel, J.), recorded no movement; the Google transfer motion remains under submission before Preska, and the next milestone in the Meta action is the September 15, 2026 initial conference before Judge Castel at 3:00 PM in Courtroom 11D. *Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence*, No. 25-2153 (3d Cir.), likewise recorded no movement, with the panel of Judges Restrepo, Montgomery-Reeves, and Bove continuing to deliberate following the June 11 oral argument.

items.body_md:
On August 11, Judge Vince Chhabria denied Meta's motion to quash subpoenas in four coordinated cases — Nos. 3:25-cv-09579, 3:26-cv-02333, 3:26-cv-03725, and 3:26-cv-04053 — ruling, without a written opinion, that the subpoenas were justified for the reasons stated in the plaintiffs' opposition briefs. The order, docketed in *Kadrey v. Meta* (N.D. Cal. No. 3:23-cv-03417) at Dkt. 807, keeps third-party discovery from multiple related proceedings on track. Judge Chhabria had already, on August 10, granted Meta's own motion for leave to serve discovery on the plaintiffs in the *Kadrey* case itself (Dkt. 806), so both sides are now simultaneously pressed into active written discovery. On August 12, the parties filed a Joint Case Management Statement (Dkt. 808), signaling that the August 14 case-management conference — now set by Clerk's Notice as a Zoom teleconference — will address the coordination of those parallel discovery obligations. The back-to-back quash denial and the joint CMC statement together indicate that pre-trial discovery in *Kadrey* and its cluster is moving on a compressed front, with the scope of permissible third-party discovery now settled in plaintiffs' favor for purposes of the coordinated subpoenas.

In *Britannica v. OpenAI* (S.D.N.Y. No. 1:26-cv-02097, Judge Sidney H. Stein), the docket recorded a Memo Endorsement at Dkt. 59 on August 12, one week after Judge Stein entered two orders setting deadlines (Dkts. 57–58, August 7) following the parties' proposed stipulation at Dkt. 56. The content of Dkt. 59 is not publicly available in secondary sources; the filing type — a memo endorsement — is a chambers signoff on a letter or stipulation and is procedural on its face, though its importance depends on what it endorsed. 
The case sits in the Southern District of New York
 and is also an associated case in the OpenAI MDL, 
with a status conference before Magistrate Judge Ona T. Wang having been held on March 10, 2026, in the MDL context.
 Until the endorsed document is retrieved, the August 12 entry is classified as procedural-but-potentially-important and held without further characterization.

In *Getty Images (US) v. Stability AI* (N.D. Cal. No. 3:25-cv-06891, Judge Trina L. Thompson), a substantive opposition brief landed at Dkt. 71 on August 12, opposing whichever pending motion drew it — the prior day's Dkt. 70, an Administrative Motion under Civil Local Rule 7-11, itself followed a pattern already established with a parallel Administrative Motion at Dkt. 68 on August 6 and an opposition at Dkt. 69 on August 10. Civil Local Rule 7-11 governs administrative motions for routine relief (seal, file under seal, extend page limits, or request a stipulation), so the pair of administrative motions with oppositions signals a collateral dispute about discovery or briefing mechanics rather than a merits filing; both the Dkt. 68/69 and Dkt. 70/71 pairs are substantive only if the underlying Administrative Motion carries a merits dimension, which the docket labels alone do not confirm. 
Getty refiled in the Northern District of California on August 14, 2025, after voluntarily dismissing the Delaware action, advancing direct copyright, DMCA §1202, and Lanham Act trademark claims
 — all of which remain at the pleadings stage given the amended answer filed at Dkt. 67 on July 2. The next confirmed scheduling marker is the Further Case Management Conference set for November 5, 2026, with a Joint CMC Statement due October 29, 2026.

*Hachette v. Google (Gemini)* (S.D.N.Y. No. 1:26-cv-05870, Judge Loretta A. Preska) and *Hachette v. Meta (Llama)* (S.D.N.Y. No. 1:26-cv-03689, Judge P. Kevin Castel) recorded no new substantive docket activity. In *Hachette v. Meta*, the next concrete milestone is the conference before Judge Castel on September 15, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. in Courtroom 11D, where Google's transfer motion and related pre-motion practice in the *Hachette v. Google* matter remain in briefing following the reply filed at Dkt. 26 on August 10. *Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence* (3d Cir. No. 25-2153) remains under submission following oral argument before a panel of Judges Restrepo, Montgomery-Reeves, and Bove on June 11, 2026; no decision has issued.

The next concrete milestone across the group is the *Kadrey* Zoom teleconference before Judge Chhabria, scheduled for August 14, 2026, at which discovery scope and coordination across the cluster are expected to be addressed.

On August 10, Judge Vince Chhabria granted Meta's administrative motion for leave to serve discovery in *Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:23-cv-03417 (N.D. Cal.), Dkt. 806 — authorizing discovery requests the court characterized as facially reasonable based on the sample RFPs and interrogatories the parties submitted. The order preserves plaintiffs' ability to challenge any individual request that "greatly exceeds" the scope of the samples, but the baseline grant is clear and unqualified. That ruling is material: it opens Meta to written discovery on the contributory-infringement amendment Judge Chhabria allowed in March, and fact discovery under the operative scheduling order closes December 18, 2026, leaving approximately four months to complete it. The same day, Dkt. 805 resolved the sealing dispute over the Dkt. 781 motion: the court granted limited redactions as specified in the Dkt. 796 declaration, but ordered Meta to file public copies of all attached documents — including entirely unredacted versions of any documents not covered by that declaration — within seven days, placing that compliance deadline on or before August 17. The transcript of Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson's August 5 hearing was docketed at Dkt. 804; it is currently restricted per General Order No. 59 pending the standard release period.

In *Hachette Book Group et al. v. Google LLC*, No. 1:26-cv-05870 (S.D.N.Y.), Judge Loretta A. Preska received the plaintiffs' reply brief at Dkt. 26, filed August 10, completing briefing on Google's letter motion for a pre-motion conference concerning a potential transfer of this action to the Northern District of California (Dkt. 21, filed August 4). Plaintiffs' opposition letter, filed August 7 by Jeffrey M. Gould of Oppenheim & Zebrak (Dkt. 25), had already closed the three-round exchange; the reply advances the transfer dispute to Judge Preska for a ruling or a conference order. The transfer question matters beyond forum logistics: Google's preferred venue is the N.D. Cal., where the parallel *In re Google Generative AI Copyright Litigation* is already pending, and consolidation there would reshape discovery coordination and potentially dilute plaintiffs' SDNY litigation choices. The Dkt. 24 pro hac vice deficiency for Benjamin Blystad Gould — missing a California Supreme Court Certificate of Good Standing — remains a ministerial open item and carries no substantive consequence.

The remaining group members were quiet. In *Hachette v. Meta (Llama)*, No. 1:26-cv-03689 (S.D.N.Y., Judge Castel), the September 15, 2026, conference on venue and Meta's anticipated transfer motion remains the next fixed event; the competing letters on the motion-to-strike question (Dkts. 90 and 92) are before Judge Castel and unresolved. *Britannica v. OpenAI*, No. 1:26-cv-02097 (Judge Stein), and *Getty Images (US) v. Stability AI*, No. 3:25-cv-06891 (N.D. Cal., Judge Thompson), recorded no substantive movement.

The next concrete milestone across the group is Meta's seven-day deadline to file the unsealed Dkt. 781 documents in *Kadrey* — on or before August 17 — followed by Judge Preska's forthcoming disposition of the Google transfer conference request in *Hachette v. Google*.

items.body_md:
On August 7, Judge Sidney H. Stein entered two deadline-setting orders (Dkt. 57 and Dkt. 58) in *Encyclopaedia Britannica, Inc. and Merriam-Webster, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc. et al.*, No. 1:26-cv-02097 (S.D.N.Y.), building on the proposed stipulation the parties filed August 5 (Dkt. 56). The docket entries are styled as utility orders, so the operative effect — whether they govern a response schedule, a service deadline, or some other procedural step — cannot be confirmed from the docket text alone; the substance will require PACER access. What the pair of orders does confirm is that Judge Stein is actively managing the schedule rather than letting the case drift. The case 
was originally filed in the Southern District of New York and concerns OpenAI's ChatGPT-based AI products
; the primary claims turn on 
allegations that OpenAI copied nearly 100,000 Britannica articles and Merriam-Webster dictionary entries without permission to train ChatGPT
, with 
additional claims for trademark violations arising from false attributions in AI responses
. The scheduling activity on August 7 is a routine procedural beat, not a substantive development, but it signals the case is moving toward an ordered pretrial posture.

Also on August 7, two filings moved in *Hachette Book Group, Inc. et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 1:26-cv-03689 (S.D.N.Y.), before Judge P. Kevin Castel. Anna M. Rennich entered an appearance for all plaintiffs (Dkt. 91), and a letter was filed at Dkt. 92, the contents of which are not visible from the docket description alone. The appearance of new counsel is a staffing addition, not a strategic inflection, but it arrives at a meaningful moment: the August 3 letter motion for leave to file a motion to strike (Dkt. 90) is pending before Judge Castel, and the court has already set a September 15, 2026 conference at 3:00 p.m. in Courtroom 11D that will include argument on Meta's transfer motion (Dkt. 89). That transfer question is the near-term gating issue for claimants — a transfer to the Northern District of California could bring this case within the orbit of Judge Chhabria, whose fair use ruling against the *Kadrey* plaintiffs last year creates an unfavorable precedent backdrop. The publisher plaintiffs here are structured to distinguish that outcome: 
the complaint alleges Meta trained its Llama models on more than 267 terabytes of copyrighted material from notorious pirate sites and masked its IP addresses to avoid detection when torrenting, stripped copyright management information from the acquired works, and abandoned legitimate licensing negotiations at Zuckerberg's direction
 — allegations framed precisely to establish willfulness and market harm that were absent from *Kadrey*. The next concrete milestone is the September 15 conference.

In *Hachette Book Group, Inc. et al. v. Google LLC*, No. 1:26-cv-05870 (S.D.N.Y.), before Judge Loretta A. Preska, the August 7 activity was procedural. A response to motion was filed at Dkt. 25, and the clerk issued a deficiency notice requiring counsel Benjamin Blystad Gould to re-file his pro hac vice application (Dkt. 24) with a Certificate of Good Standing from the Supreme Court of California — the only missing item. The underlying $200.00 fee receipt (ANYSDC-33253987) stands; only the certificate needs to be supplied. Judge Preska had granted three other pro hac vice admissions the prior day (Dkt. 23: Derek W. Loeser, Paul J. Sampson, and Chris Nathaniel Ryder), so this is a cure-and-refile matter, not a contested one. The pro hac vice build-out across both Hachette cases — *Google* and *Meta* — reflects the same plaintiffs' counsel team (led by Keller Loeser) staffing up across parallel fronts.

In *Kadrey et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.*, No. 3:23-cv-03417 (N.D. Cal.), before Judge Vince Chhabria, the August 7 docket produced duplicate transcript orders (Dkt. 802 and 803) for the July 31, 2026 proceedings before Judge Chhabria, ordered by court reporter Layli Phillips. This follows the August 5 discovery hearing before Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson (Dkt. 799) at which counsel for both parties appeared via Zoom, and the two transcript orders filed August 6 covering that Magistrate hearing (Dkt. 800 and 801). The duplication of the Dkt. 802/803 transcript request appears administrative. Judge Chhabria granted plaintiffs leave to add the contributory infringement claim in March 2026 (Dkt. 700), noting that 
regardless of whether the plaintiffs were allowed to add the contributory infringement claim, Meta would be required to litigate it given the parallel *Entrepreneur Media* case, which already includes that claim and shares a discovery schedule
. The active discovery posture before Magistrate Judge Hixson, evidenced by the August 5 hearing and the transcript orders that followed, is consistent with that shared schedule running.

*Getty Images (US), Inc. v. Stability AI, Inc. et al.*, No. 3:25-cv-06891 (N.D. Cal.), before Judge Trina L. Thompson, and *Thomson Reuters Enterprise Centre GmbH et al. v. Ross Intelligence, Inc.*, No. 25-2153 (3d Cir.), were quiet. The Third Circuit panel in *Thomson Reuters* — Judges Restrepo, Montgomery-Reeves, and Bove — heard oral argument June 11 and directed the parties to file a transcript by June 25 (Dkt. 205). No ruling has issued publicly. The next concrete milestone across the active dockets is the September 15, 2026 conference in *Hachette v. Meta (Llama)* before Judge Castel.
